correctness.rationale: For the SPD unit-diagonal Gram G, the sharp one-step expected squared-error gain is the least eigenvalue of the affine information matrix. Group symmetry reduces the global maximum without presupposing uniqueness. The repeated-row contrast eigenvalue is (1-alpha)q; the remaining two eigenvalues equal those of the explicit 2x2 M(r). Its smaller eigenvalue satisfies a global determinant-square certificate and is concave via a fixed-vector affine representation. A single crossing gives the exact beta_c transition and both branch formulas. A bottom-eigenvector kernel argument proves uniqueness even against asymmetric sampling laws, including the beta=0 boundary. Executed verification code independently checks 270 spectral parameter cases, 6480 random probability laws, 11 numerical optimizers and 6 exact/symbolic identities. These finite tests are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The new claim evaluates, rather than merely restates, the previously known worst-direction eigenvalue SDP for sampling. The closed two-branch formulas and sharp coherence threshold hold for all repeated-block sizes and all admissible beta, and arbitrary asymmetric optimizers are excluded. The inspected primary texts establish the general contraction/SDP framework but do not state a theorem implying this exact evaluation. General and specialized earlier coverage remains a residual risk, not proof of uniqueness in the literature.

value.rationale: Repeated mutually correlated measurements with one differently correlated exceptional measurement form a natural and interpretable finite-measurement design. The exact optimizer determines when group contrasts versus coupled exceptional-mode geometry controls guaranteed projection improvement; it gives a sharp threshold, nontrivial deviation from conventional uniform/norm sampling, unique design, and an infinite-dimensional-size family. This is a motivated structural design result rather than an arbitrary finite computation. The nontrivial exact 35-percent class of gains and uniform-only-at-beta=alpha criterion clarify practical allocation.
